course_title: Honours Research Project in Veterinary Technology
course_description:
This course allows veterinary technicians to undertake their own research project under the supervision of an experienced academic. With the help of their supervisor, students will design a study, collect and analyse data and write up their study as a small thesis. They will also present their study as a seminar to their peers and academics. This will provide the student with an appreciation of the research process and the concept of evidence-based medicine that underpins clinical practice. Students also receive training in research skills that enables them to pursue further research study.

Students commencing in Semester 1 full-time enrol in VETS6631 for 2 consecutive semesters. Students commencing in Semester 2 full-time enrol in VETS6632 for 2 consecutive semesters.

In Honours Research Projects, there are no formal lectures. You are expected to work on your research project and prepare drafts of your thesis and seminars under the guidance of your supervisor(s). The research project extends over two semesters full-time and is written up as a small thesis that includes an abstract, an introduction, a review of the relevant literature, a description of the methodology used, documentation of experimental results, a discussion of experimental results with respect to other published findings, a conclusion and a list of references used.

restrictions: Enrolment restricted to Bachelor of Veterinary Technology (Honours) students.

course_aims: The general aim of this postgraduate research program is that students complete theses of merit. This course should encourage you to develop and demonstrate capabilities for critical thought and independent research. You will learn how to conceive, design, carry out and communicate science through the development and practice of sound research skills together with the presentation of your results.

learning_outcomes.description: Cultivate and demonstrate the skills, knowledge and attitudes required to perform self-directed, original, independent, ethical research.
Apply skills in communication, time management, problem solving and organisation to meet project milestones and work effectively in a research team.
Objectively analyse current knowledge in your field and use innovative and novel approaches to address gaps in knowledge and/or revise methodologies.
Apply detailed understanding, and demonstrate developing mastery of your research field to evaluate literature and optimise project design, critically and objectively.
Utilise appropriate experimental design and statistical analysis to critically analyse and draw accurate conclusions from your research.
Summarise and communicate your research effectively to a broad scientific audience, in written (thesis presentation) and verbal (seminar presentation) formats.

Students should seek detailed guidance from their supervisor (s) for the development and review of their seminar. Students must prepare a seminar abstract suitable for advertising the seminar throughout SVS, have this reviewed by their advisors, and provide the abstract to the course coordinator 2 weeks before their agreed presentation date. See the SVS BVetTech Honours handbook on the course Blackboard site for further information. A template for the seminar is also available on Blackboard. This honours seminar is worth 25% of the assessment, and it will be assessed by the thesis examiners or others as appointed by the course coordinator. Deferral or extension
You may be able to defer this exam .
Students must be available for their examinations on the scheduled date, time, and campus of their course enrolment. The exam format is determined by the Course Coordinator and may include written (paper-based, online, or digital), practical, oral, or other timed assessments (such as quizzes).
If you are unable to sit for your original examination, you may be eligible for a deferred examination. To apply, you must demonstrate that unavoidable circumstances prevented you from attending your exam. If this is not possible, you can apply for a one-off discretionary deferred exam. All requests for deferred examinations MUST include supporting documentation. For more information, including acceptable evidence and application instructions, please visit my.UQ Deferring an Exam .
Please note that there are no provisions to defer an already-deferred exam. You must be available to sit your deferred examination at the allocated time.
Students who submit five or more deferral requests within a twelve-month period will be contacted with advice on the services and support available within the University.

assessment_details.task_description: Students will submit a final Honours thesis. The thesis will include an abstract, introduction (detailing previous work and the aims and hypotheses of the current study), methodology, results, discussion (including conclusions) and references. Details on the format and content requirements of the honours thesis are available on the course Blackboard and in the SVS BVetTech honours handbook. The final thesis will be examined by two examiners – normally, this will be conducted by two internal examiners or one internal examiner and one external to the School of Veterinary Science (SVS). The percentage mark awarded will be the average of the two examiners' marks. Thesis marks will be subject to a moderation process conducted by the course coordinator or a discipline expert nominated by the course coordinator if they differ by 10% or more. A third examiner will be used and the final thesis mark an average of the three marks. A mark of no less than 50% in the honours thesis is required to pass the course. An overall mark of no less than 50% is required to pass the course. Read full task description Hide full task description

A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
You are required to submit assessable items on time.
If you fail to meet the submission deadline for any assessment item, then 10% of the maximum possible mark for the assessment item (assessment ‘marked from’ value) will be deducted as a late penalty for every day (or part day) late after the due date.
For example, if you submit your assignment 1 hour late, you will be penalised 10%; if your assignment is 24.5 hours late, you will be penalised 20% (because it is late by one 24-hour period plus part of another 24-hour period).
10% will be deducted per day for up to 7 calendar days, at which point your submission will receive a mark of zero (0) unless an extension has been approved.

learning_activities.topic: Demonstrate self directed learning Students will demonstrate self-directed learning by independently identifying relevant learning needs, sourcing appropriate scholarly and professional resources, and engaging with material beyond scheduled teaching activities. This activity supports students to take responsibility for their own learning, manage their time effectively, reflect on gaps in knowledge or skills, and apply new information to veterinary science, clinical decision-making, research or professional practice contexts. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Review and critique published scientific literature Students will review and critique published scientific literature relevant to veterinary science and animal health. This activity will develop students’ ability to read research papers critically, identify the strengths and limitations of study design, interpret results, assess the quality of evidence, and consider how research findings may be applied in clinical, industry or research contexts. Students will be expected to discuss key findings, evaluate the validity of conclusions, and reflect on the relevance of the literature to evidence-based veterinary practice. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Devise, plan and conduct an Honours research project Students will devise, plan and conduct an Honours research project under academic supervision. This activity will develop students’ capacity to formulate a research question, design an appropriate methodology, consider ethical and practical requirements, collect and manage data, analyse findings, and interpret results in relation to the existing literature. Students will progressively build research independence, problem-solving skills, scientific judgement and professional communication skills through the completion of a substantial research project. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Develop research literacy through participation in research seminars Students will develop research literacy through participation in research seminars delivered by academic staff, researchers, peers and external experts. This activity will expose students to a range of research questions, methodologies, analytical approaches and disciplinary perspectives relevant to veterinary science. Through active listening, questioning and reflection, students will build their ability to interpret research presentations, evaluate evidence, recognise features of effective scientific communication, and situate their own Honours research within the broader research landscape. Learning outcomes: L06

Work in a laboratory environment (optional) Students may have the opportunity to work in a laboratory environment as part of their Honours research project, where this is relevant to the project design. This activity will support the development of practical research skills, including safe laboratory practice, appropriate use of equipment, sample handling, data collection, record keeping, and adherence to relevant ethical, biosafety and workplace health and safety requirements. Students will develop an understanding of how laboratory methods contribute to research quality, reliability and interpretation of results. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

Collect field based data (optional) Students may have the opportunity to collect field-based data as part of their Honours research project, where this is relevant to the project design. This activity will support the development of practical research skills in real-world veterinary, animal production, wildlife, clinical or industry settings. Students will develop skills in planning fieldwork, collecting accurate and reliable data, maintaining appropriate records, managing samples or observations, and working safely and professionally in variable field conditions. The activity will also reinforce the importance of ethical approval, biosecurity, animal welfare, workplace health and safety, and data quality in applied research. Learning outcomes: L01
